lines.japanese: コーヒーのにおいと共に目覚めた。
lines.english: I awoke to the smell of coffee.

lines.japanese: まぶたを開けると今日もアレキサンダーの便所──
lines.english: I opened my eyes to find myself once again in Alexander's bathroom—

lines.japanese: ──じゃねえや。あれ？
lines.english: —no, wait. I wasn't. Huh?

lines.japanese: 目の前にはほとんど口をつけてないカップが残っている。
lines.english: An almost untouched cup sat in front of me.

lines.japanese: 時計を確認すると、時刻は２２時ちょい過ぎ。
lines.english: The clock read a little past ten at night.

lines.japanese: なんだ、あの糞ワシ。今日はアレキサンダー休みなのか？　まさかバイトも行かねーで、ぶらぶら時間つぶしてたわけじゃねーだろうな。
lines.english: What was that shit-eagle doing? Was Alexander closed today? Don't tell me he'd skipped his shift and spent all that time wandering around.

lines.japanese: それとも、もう辞めたのか。
lines.english: Or had he quit already?

lines.japanese: だったら俺から言うことは何もない。悲しいが、俺たちに長期のバイトは向いてない。いずれ居場所がなくなることは想定の範囲内だったはず。
lines.english: If so, I had nothing to say. Sad fact was, long-term employment didn't suit us. We'd always known the day would come when there was no place for him there.

lines.japanese: だよな、鷲介。まさかおまえ、そんなことで挫けちゃいないだろうな。
lines.english: Right, Shusuke? You haven't let a thing like that break you, have you?

lines.japanese: やつの残していった黒豆しぼり汁を一気に喉へ流しこむ。中途半端なぬるさ。おまけにクソ苦げえ。砂糖ぐらい入れろや見栄っ張りが、ブッ殺すぞアノヤロウ。
lines.english: I tossed the black-bean juice he'd left behind straight down my throat. Half-assedly lukewarm. Bitter as fuck, too. Put some sugar in it, you posturing bastard. I'll kill you.

lines.japanese: 俺は店の扉を開けはなち、夜の街へ踏みだした。
lines.english: I flung open the restaurant door and stepped out into the city night.

lines.japanese: 現場仕事が始まるまでの中途半端な時間を、ヤナポリ広場で潰す。
lines.english: I killed the awkward stretch before my shift at Yanapoli Plaza.

lines.japanese: 夜の柳木原は、今日もマン・ウォッチングがおもしろい。
lines.english: Man-watching in Yanagihara at night was fun as ever.

lines.japanese: 前髪だけべたべたなウェット感を出した刈上げ小僧は、銀細工の露天商に言いくるめられていた。
lines.english: A kid with shaved sides and only his bangs slicked into a wet look was being sweet-talked by a street vendor selling silver jewelry.

lines.japanese: 俺はそいつが千円札四枚でくすんだ銀色の指輪を買いあげていったのを見届けてから、ほくほく顔の店主を冷やかすために近付いていった。
lines.english: I watched him pay four thousand yen for a tarnished silver ring, then went over to heckle the beaming vendor.

lines.japanese: 「おう、おっさん、いま売りつけた指輪なんだけど。こないだはボンバヘッドな頭の外人ねーちゃんに二千円で売ってなかったっけ。モンゴロイドなめんなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey, old man. That ring you just pushed on him—you sold the same one to some foreign chick with a bomb of a hairdo for two thousand the other day, didn't you? Don't think you can fleece an Asian, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「あらやだ、ドラちゃん。声が聞こえちゃうから、そのお話をするのはあと５分待ってちょうだい。いまの男の子、いいリピーターになりそうなのよ」
lines.english: “Oh, Drac, darling. He can still hear you, so wait five minutes before you bring that up. That boy looks like excellent repeat business.”

lines.japanese: やつはぶっとい唇にぶっとい人差し指を当てて、シィッ！　と口蓋音を鳴らした。見開いた目とすぼめた口。相も変わらぬオーバーアクションに、俺は不覚にも愛嬌を覚えてしまった。
lines.english: Martinez put one thick index finger to thick lips and made a sharp *shhh!* against the roof of the mouth. Eyes wide, lips puckered. Same huge gestures as always, and damn it, I found them cute.

lines.japanese: 「ま、退院おめっとさん」
lines.english: “Well, congrats on getting out.”

lines.japanese: あの事件から一週間弱。刺されたマルチネスは出血量のわりに傷が浅く、また驚くべき強靭さを持ちあわせていたおかげで、座ってさえいれば店番できる程度には回復していた。
lines.english: It had been just under a week since the incident. The stab wound was shallow despite all the blood, and Martinez was tough as hell, so she'd recovered enough to mind the stall as long as she stayed seated.

lines.japanese: 「日本の病院は雌犬くさくてダメね。一ヵ月もあんなところにいたら、男の芯が根元から腐ってしまうわ」
lines.english: “Japanese hospitals reek of bitches. Spend a month in one and a man's very core rots from the root up.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、元から腐ってんだろ。つかおまえ、腐ったって問題ないじゃん。つか、まだ付いてたの」
lines.english: “Yours was rotten to begin with. Besides, what would it matter to you? Wait—you still had one?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ！　デリカシーのない男ね。付いてるとか付いてないとか露骨なこと言わないでちょうだい」
lines.english: “My! What an indelicate man. Please don't talk so explicitly about what I may or may not have attached.”

lines.japanese: 「つか、入院ついでに取ってもらえばよかったのに」
lines.english: “Should’ve had it removed while you were in there.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫、心の中には付いてないわ」
lines.english: “Don’t worry. I don’t have one in my heart.”

lines.japanese: 「つうかさ、前々から疑問だったんだけど、おまえリアルにそっちなの。カマくさい日本語使ってるだけで、中身はストレートなんじゃねえの」
lines.english: “Listen, I've wondered about this for a while. Are you actually that way? Or do you just speak campy Japanese while you're straight underneath?”

lines.japanese: 「フフフ、試してみる？」
lines.english: “Mmm. Care to find out?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいい」
lines.english: “No, thanks.”

lines.japanese: 「つれないわねえ。アタシとドラちゃんはいいお友達だと思ってたのに」
lines.english: “How cold. And here I thought you and I were such dear friends.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからじゃん」
lines.english: “That's exactly why.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、友達の趣味がちょっとぐらい特殊だからって、それで見方が変わるわけでもねーし。どっちでもいいよ」
lines.english: “A friend having tastes a little out of the ordinary doesn't change how I see him. Either way, I don't care.”

lines.japanese: 「んまあドラちゃん！　偉い、アタシ感動したわ！　ふところの広い日本人もいたのね！」
lines.english: “Oh, Drac! How admirable! I'm moved! So there really are broad-minded Japanese men!”

lines.japanese: 「うわっ、ちょ、抱きつくな。偏見はねーけど、共感はしてねえよ。やめろバカ、俺に被害が及ばないかぎりってのが大前提に決まってんだろ。それ以上近づいたら舌噛むぞコラ」
lines.english: “Whoa—hey, don't hug me. I've got no prejudice, but that doesn't mean I relate. Stop, idiot. Obviously this arrangement depends on it never becoming my problem. One step closer and I'll bite my tongue.”

lines.japanese: 「んもう、水臭いこと言うんじゃないわよ。共に強く生きていきましょう、セクシャル・マイノリティ同士」
lines.english: “Oh, don't be so distant. Let us be strong together, one sexual minority to another.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、人聞き悪いから、冗談でも俺になんらかの特殊な性癖があるがごとく纏めンのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Hey, hey. People can hear you. Even as a joke, quit lumping me in like I've got some freaky kink.”

lines.japanese: 「フフ、隠さなくていいわよ。話はぜんぶプラチナに聞いてるから」
lines.english: “Mmm, no need to hide it. Platinum told me everything.”

lines.japanese: 「彼は言った、ドラは好む子供を」
lines.english: “He said it: Drac likes children.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 声のした方に振りむくと子供が立っていた。例の事件以来だ。
lines.english: I turned toward the voice and found a child standing there. I hadn't seen her since the incident.

lines.japanese: 「おー、アリス。なんだよ、いたンなら言えよ。いつからいたの」
lines.english: “Hey, Alice. If you were here, say something. How long've you been around?”

lines.japanese: 「ジャストナウ」
lines.english: “Just now.”

lines.japanese: 「アタシが呼んだのよ、さっきドラちゃんの顔を見つけたときに」
lines.english: “I called her over when I spotted you a minute ago.”

lines.japanese: 「おお。で、どうなの。元気だったの」
lines.english: “Oh. So, how've you been? Doing okay?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、私はいちじるしく元気だ。おびただしく調子がよい。目を覆うほどの健康である」
lines.english: “Yes. I am conspicuously healthy. My condition is multitudinously excellent. My health is positively blinding.”

lines.japanese: 「おー、相変わらず日本語は変だけど、元気なら良かった良かった。うん、まあ、良かった」
lines.english: “Good. Your Japanese is still weird as hell, but if you're healthy, good. That's good.”

lines.japanese: ちょっと迷ったものの、俺はあの件について触れないことにした。
lines.english: I hesitated briefly, then decided not to mention the incident.

lines.japanese: 無事ことなきを得たマルチネスはすでに自ら笑い話の種にもしてるけど、子供の小さな目には相当ショッキングな光景だったろう。忘れられるなら忘れてほしいものだ。
lines.english: Martinez had come through safely and was already making jokes about it. Seen through a child’s eyes, though, it must have been a terrible sight. If Alice could forget it, I hoped she would.

lines.japanese: いまこうして見ても、心なしか金髪碧眼の少女はかつてより弱く儚げに見え……いや、違うな、実際いつもより微妙に身だしなみよくしてるのか。
lines.english: Looking at her now, the blond, blue-eyed girl somehow seemed weaker and more fragile than before... no, that wasn't it. Was she actually just a little better groomed than usual?

lines.japanese: 「なにアリス、今日はやけに毛先まとまってンじゃん。枝毛もねえな。どーした、色気付いちゃって」
lines.english: “What's this, Alice? Your ends are all neat today. Not a split hair in sight. What happened, getting glamorous on me?”

lines.japanese: 「あら、そんな細かいとこに気付くなんて、まあよく見てること」
lines.english: “My, noticing a detail that small. You certainly do look at her closely.”

lines.japanese: 「彼は魅了されている私に。なぜなら、彼は好む子供を」
lines.english: “He is captivated by me. For he prefers children.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーよ。全然ねーよ。つか、またそういう流れかよ。なに。今度はプラチナがなんて言ったわけ」
lines.english: “Yeah, no. Not even close. And we’re doing this again? What? What’d Platinum tell you this time?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラちゃんが小さい女の子と付き合ってるって」
lines.english: “That Drac is dating a very little girl.”

lines.japanese: 「あゴメン、それはホントだわ」
lines.english: “Oh. Sorry. That part's true.”

lines.japanese: <8>\「ホントなのかよ！」
lines.english: “IT'S TRUE?!”

lines.japanese: 思わずおっさん声が飛びだすほどマルチネスを驚かせてしまったようだ。その巨体で咄嗟にアリスの身を隠している。いや、隠すなよ。襲わねーよ、子供なんか。
lines.english: Martinez was startled enough to drop into an old man's bellow. That massive body instantly moved to shield Alice. Hey, don't hide her. I wasn't about to attack a kid.

lines.japanese: 「小さい女って身長の話だから。ほら、マルチネスも一度会ってンじゃん。あいつだよ」
lines.english: “Little as in short. Martinez, you've met her before. You know who.”

lines.japanese: 「んまあ！　やっぱりあの子なのね、クキィーッ！」
lines.english: “My! So it was that girl after all—rrrgh!”

lines.japanese: やつはジャージをへそまでまくり上げて、その裾をぎりぎり噛んでいる。へえ、その悔しさ表現って、日本固有の文化じゃなかったんだ……。
lines.english: Martinez had the sweatshirt yanked up to the navel and was biting the hem for all it was worth. Huh. Guess that frustration move wasn't Japanese-only after all.

lines.japanese: 「ふーッ！　まったく、あの子とは一度じっくり話しあわなきゃならないわね」
lines.english: “Hmph! I shall have to sit that girl down for a very serious talk.”

lines.japanese: 「私も参加するだろう、その会議に。なぜならそれは重大な関心事、ミートゥー」
lines.english: “I too will participate in this conference. For it is a matter of grave concern. Me too.”

lines.japanese: 「んまっ、身内にまでアタシのライバルが！？　これはジャパニーズ慣用句で言うところの、昨日の友イズ今日の敵ってやつね！」
lines.english: “My! A rival in my own family? As the Japanese idiom says: yesterday's friend is today's enemy!”

lines.japanese: 「油断ビカム大敵」
lines.english: “Carelessness becomes the greatest enemy.”

lines.japanese: 「まったく、雌犬に手をしゃぶられるとはこのことじゃない。上等よ、尻の骨をまくって逃げるがいいわ」
lines.english: “Honestly, so this is what they mean by having a bitch lick the hand that feeds her! Fine! Tuck the bones of your bottom and flee!”

lines.japanese: 「ねえよ。我が国にそんな慣用句ねえよ」
lines.english: “No. There are no idioms like that in this country.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラは盗んだ、とんでもないもの。それは我々の心だ」
lines.english: “Drac stole something terrible. He stole our hearts.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえよ。もう色々ねえよ」
lines.english: “No. So many parts of that don't exist.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、つれないわねドラちゃん。アタシはすっかり過去の女ってわけね。いいわ、それなら最後にこのアクセサリーを買っていきなさい。なに、大丈夫。金がなければ担保いらずの消費者金融を紹介してやるから」
lines.english: “Ah, so cold, Drac. I suppose I'm yesterday's woman now. Fine. Then buy this accessory as our final farewell. Don't worry—if you're broke, I'll introduce you to an unsecured consumer lender.”

lines.japanese: 「あなたは思ってはならない、ただで帰れるなどと」
lines.english: “You must not imagine that you will be allowed to leave without paying.”

lines.japanese: 「シャラップ」
lines.english: “Shut it.”

lines.japanese: 俺はサムライ魂を発揮して、恐喝行為に屈することなく、露店の売り物をＳＨＡＫＥした。
lines.english: I summoned my samurai spirit, refused to submit to extortion, and gave the stall's merchandise a SHAKE.

lines.japanese: 「ノオォーっ！　何さらすんじゃこのサル、いてこましたろか──」
lines.english: “Nooo! What the hell are you doing, you ape? I'll beat your—”

lines.japanese: 「──シット！　それどころじゃないわ、アリス撤収よ」
lines.english: “—shit! No time for this. Alice, retreat!”

lines.japanese: リトル日米紛争が勃発しかけたものの、交番から不審顔の警官が出てきたところでマルチネスはあたふたと店じまいを始めた。
lines.english: A little Japan-America war almost broke out, but then a cop stepped out of the police box looking suspicious, and Martinez hurriedly started packing up.

lines.japanese: 無許可の露天商は逃げ脚がはやい。
lines.english: Unlicensed street vendors knew how to make themselves scarce.

lines.japanese: 駅から流れてくる人の波がピークを過ぎたころ、俺たちはアリスをタクシー乗り場まで連れていった。
lines.english: Once the wave of people from the station had passed its peak, we walked Alice to the taxi stand.

lines.japanese: 「ありガトうございます」
lines.english: “Thank yoo very much.”

lines.japanese: 乗りこむ間際、やつは比較的まともな日本語で言った。
lines.english: Just before climbing in, she spoke comparatively normal Japanese.

lines.japanese: 「私はあなたのおこないにとても感謝をしています」
lines.english: “I feel the greatest gratitude for your conduct.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: いや、まともじゃないか。たかだか日常会話で、そこまで大げさな言い回しをするネイティブはいない。
lines.english: No—hardly normal. No native speaker dressed up everyday conversation in language that grand.

lines.japanese: まあ、要は「どうもね。じゃあ」的なことを言いたいんだろうけど、どんな学びごとでも中級者ぐらいってのは張りきり過ぎてしまうものだ。
lines.english: She probably meant something like, *Thanks. See you.* But anyone halfway through learning something tends to overdo it.

lines.japanese: 「私は感謝しています──あなたに感謝しています」
lines.english: “I am grateful. To you, I am grateful.”

lines.japanese: 「もし無ければ──もし出会いが無ければ──もしあなたとの出会いがなければ、私はまだ日本人を嫌いつづけていたでしょう」
lines.english: “Had there not been—had there been no encounter—had I not encountered you, I would still have continued to hate the Japanese.”

lines.japanese: 倒置法にならないよう、ちらちらカンニングペーパーらしきものを確認しながら続けるアリス。前もって準備していたのか、紙面には手書きのローマ字がびっしり埋まっていた。
lines.english: Alice continued, stealing glances at what looked like a cheat sheet as she labored to keep her word order straight. She must have prepared in advance; the page was dense with handwritten romanization.

lines.japanese: 子供なりの独学で、一生懸命にこんな小っぽけな島国の言葉を勉強してくれたんだろう。なんとなく嬉しいじゃないか。マルチネスもスマイリーな保護者ヅラで見守っていた。
lines.english: She must have taught herself, working hard to learn the language of this tiny island nation. Somehow, that made me happy. Martinez watched with the beaming face of a guardian.

lines.japanese: 「日本へ来たとき、私はこの国の文化や風土に、進んで迎合することはしませんでした。なぜなら、私は私の母が待っているところの本国へ帰りたいと望んでいたからです」
lines.english: “When I came to Japan, I did not willingly adapt myself to the culture or climate of this nation. This was because I desired to return to my home country, where my mother was waiting.”

lines.japanese: 「すなわち、日本での生活が肌に合わないと認識させれば、私の父は私を本国へ還すだろうと予想したのです。しかしながら、想定しなかったことに、私の父はほとんど私の生活に興味を寄せませんでした」
lines.english: “In other words, I thought that if I made it clear life in Japan did not suit me, my father would send me home. Yet, contrary to my expectation, my father took almost no interest in my life.”

lines.japanese: 「私は、私の父の任期が終わるまで、日本に留まるしかないと悟りました。やむを得ず、方針を変え、私は日本での生活を可能なかぎり楽しむことにしました」
lines.english: “I perceived that I had no option but to remain in Japan until my father's term of office concluded. Compelled by circumstance, I altered policy and determined to enjoy life in Japan to the maximum possible extent.”

lines.japanese: 「ところが、私はそのときまで日本の少女たちを敬遠し、また反発をしていたので、もはや彼女たちの私的な共同体に参加することが困難でした。家でも学校でも、私は毎日とても寂しい感情を感じていました」
lines.english: “However, until that time I had kept Japanese girls at a distance and opposed them, making participation in their private communities difficult. At home and at school, I experienced very lonely emotions every day.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなとき、ふと街角で声をかけてくれた日本人。それがアナタなんだって、ドラちゃん」
lines.english: “And then, one day, a Japanese man spoke to her on a street corner. That man was you, Drac.”

lines.japanese: 「私の日本人のともだちは、皆あなたを介したひとびとです。あなたと、あなたを介したひとびとによって、私は孤独を免れることができました」
lines.english: “All my Japanese friends are people I met through you. Thanks to you, and to those I met through you, I was able to escape loneliness.”

lines.japanese: 「したがって私は礼を述べます。ありがとうございました。また逢いましょう」
lines.english: “Therefore, I state my thanks. Thank you very much. Let us meet again.”

lines.japanese: アリスは日本式に腰を折った。慣れないお辞儀がなんだか微笑ましくて、俺はやつの頭に手を置いた。
lines.english: Alice bent at the waist in a Japanese bow. Something about her unpracticed attempt made me smile, and I rested a hand on her head.

lines.japanese: 「おう、分かりやすかったぞ。ずいぶん上手くなったじゃねーか、日本語」
lines.english: “Yeah. Easy to understand. Your Japanese's gotten a whole lot better.”

lines.japanese: 「でもなアリス、そういう堅ッ苦しいのは酒の入った夜中の居酒屋か、送別会のときだけでいいんだ」
lines.english: “But listen, Alice. Save stiff speeches like that for drunken late nights at a bar, or a farewell party.”

lines.japanese: 「ソウ、ソウベッツ・カイン……？」
lines.english: “Yes. Farewell... party...?”

lines.japanese: やつが首をひねりながらポケット辞書をめくりだしたので、取りあげてランドセルへブチこむ。
lines.english: She cocked her head and started leafing through a pocket dictionary. I confiscated it and stuffed it into her schoolbag.

lines.japanese: 「いいんだよ。俺らは友達なんだから、そういうときは一言でいいの。一言……そうだな、おまえみたいな良い子なら、いいか、こうだ」
lines.english: “Never mind. We're friends. At times like this, one phrase is enough. One phrase... Let's see. For a good kid like you, it goes like this.”

lines.japanese: 「またね」
lines.english: “See you around.”

lines.japanese: 目つぶしピースも添えた。その指先をきょとんと見つめるアリス。
lines.english: I threw in an eye-poke peace sign. Alice stared blankly at my fingertips.

lines.japanese: 「知ってる。意味はシーユーアゲイン」
lines.english: “I know. Its meaning is 'see you again.'”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ話は早ええ。別れ際なんてのは、そんぐれーでいンだよ。分かったか」
lines.english: “Then we're all set. That's all friends need when they part. Got it?”

lines.japanese: 日本の──じゃないな、俺の流儀を教えていたら、横から俺の肩に触れる黒い手があった。
lines.english: I was teaching her the Japanese—no, *my*—way when a dark hand touched my shoulder.

lines.japanese: 「ドラちゃん、後ろのお客さん待ってるから、ね、そろそろ……」
lines.english: “Drac, darling, the customers behind us are waiting. So perhaps it's about time...”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「まいがー」
lines.english: “My God.”

lines.japanese: 苛立たしげな列の後続に気づいて、アリスはいそいそとタクシーに乗りこんだ。
lines.english: Noticing the irritated line behind her, Alice hurried into the taxi.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、またね」
lines.english: “Drac. See you around.”

lines.japanese: 「ん。またな」
lines.english: “Yeah. See you.”

lines.japanese: そして蒼い瞳の子供は、紫色の空が広がる大人の街から去っていった。
lines.english: And the blue-eyed child left the grown-up city beneath its violet sky.

lines.japanese: そのあとマルチネスがたばこを吸いたいというので、地下鉄入口裏の指定喫煙所へ移動した。
lines.english: Afterward Martinez wanted a cigarette, so we moved to the designated smoking area behind the subway entrance.

lines.japanese: 一本目を半分ほど喫したあたりで、やつは夜空に煙を立てながら突然つぶやいた。
lines.english: Halfway through the first cigarette, Martinez suddenly murmured, smoke climbing into the night.

lines.japanese: 「とは言っても、またの機会はねえかもな」
lines.english: “That said, there may not be another time.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、目の前の見飽きた外人が発した声だとは気付かなかった。なんだこいつ、いきなり男くさい声で。つか、やっぱ普通の日本語しゃべれンじゃねーかこの野郎。
lines.english: For a second I didn't realize that voice came from the familiar foreigner in front of me. What was with the sudden manly voice? So the bastard could speak normal Japanese after all.

lines.japanese: 「あら。やあねえ、そんな驚いちゃって。いつもと違うアリスの様子から、薄々わかったんじゃなくて？」
lines.english: “My. Don't look so startled. Didn't the change in Alice give you some idea?”

lines.japanese: おっさんはまたおばはんに戻っておどけた。
lines.english: The old man slipped back into his auntie voice and played coy.

lines.japanese: 「あの子に口止めされてたけど、もういいでしょう。あの子、おそらくもうここには来ないわ」
lines.english: “She made me promise not to tell you, but I think it’s all right now. She probably won’t come here again.”

lines.japanese: 「……マジか」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「そうね。正しくは『来られない』だけど」
lines.english: “Yes. More precisely, she *can't*.”

lines.japanese: 「どういうこと」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「あの子ね、先週アタシが入院したあの日から、実は家の外に一歩も出してもらえなかったの」
lines.english: “Since the day I was hospitalized last week, Alice hasn't been allowed one step outside the house.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。誰に」
lines.english: “Why? Who's stopping her?”

lines.japanese: 「あの子、外交官のお嬢さんだもの、本来はガチガチの箱入りなのよ」
lines.english: “She is a diplomat's daughter. Ordinarily, she's kept under lock and key.”

lines.japanese: 「皮肉なものね。仕事仕事で娘のことが見えなくなっていた親の目が、あんな事件でようやく本来向くべきところへ向いたってわけ」
lines.english: Pretty ironic, huh? A parent so buried in work he couldn't see his daughter finally got his eyes pointed where they should've been because of an incident like that.

lines.japanese: 「いずれ自宅謹慎は解けるでしょうけど、学校には専属の送迎が付くみたい。要は監視よね。娘が治安の悪いところで、よからぬ若者たちと交遊しないかを取りしまる」
lines.english: Her house arrest will probably end eventually, but it sounds like she'll have a personal ride to and from school. Basically surveillance, right? Making sure their daughter doesn't hang around bad neighborhoods with the wrong crowd.

lines.japanese: 「よからぬ若者たち」
lines.english: “Improper young people.”

lines.japanese: はいはい。まあ、そりゃあよ。たしかにお上品でも、家柄がいいわけでも、学があるわけでもねーけどよ。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Fine. Maybe we weren't refined, well-born, or educated.

lines.japanese: 「はん、勝手に言ってろ。なあ？　この際、おとんは関係ねーだろよ。問題は娘だろ、あいつ自身の気持ちだろうよ。ガキが誰と遊ぶかなんてガキの決めることだ、大人のシャシャるとこじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “Hah. Let 'em say what they like. Her old man has nothing to do with it. What matters is the girl—what *she* wants. Kids decide who they play with. Adults got no business barging in.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね。私も一面的にはその通りだと思うわ」
lines.english: “Yes. From one point of view, I think that's true.”

lines.japanese: マルチネスは俺に同調して、一度は渋面で頷いてみせた。しかしたばこを一吸いすると、ゆっくり微笑みながらかぶりを振った。
lines.english: Martinez nodded once, grimly agreeing. Then came a drag on the cigarette, a gentle smile, and a slow shake of the head.

lines.japanese: 「でも子供の目は小さいの。どんなに賢い子でも、見えてることはあまりに少ないのよ」
lines.english: “But a child's eyes are small. No matter how clever the child, there is far too much they cannot see.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、たとえ横暴と思われようとも、親が導いてあげなきゃならないときもあるわ。そんなときは親だって辛いのよ」
lines.english: “That is why there are times a parent must guide them, even if it seems tyrannical. It hurts the parent too.”

lines.japanese: 滑稽なはずのオネエ口調が、不思議なくらい自然と沁みこんでくる。
lines.english: The camp affectation ought to have sounded ridiculous. Instead, the words sank into me with uncanny ease.

lines.japanese: そしてこぼれそうに大きな黒目は、紫色の空の彼方を見上げていた。やつの流暢な日本語は、ここより遥か離れた、どこか彼方の空へ送られているような気がした。
lines.english: His huge dark eyes, almost spilling over, lifted toward the far side of the violet sky. It felt as though his fluent Japanese were meant for some other sky, far away from ours.

lines.japanese: しかし、それはさほど長くなかった。ぎゅっ、ぎゅっと丹念にたばこを揉み消すうち、やつのギョロ目はまた紫色の空の下を捉えていた。
lines.english: But it did not last long. As Martinez carefully ground out the cigarette—press, press—the bulging eyes returned to the world beneath the violet sky.

lines.japanese: 「ねえドラちゃん、アナタはアリスぐらいの歳だった自分を覚えていて？」
lines.english: “Tell me, Drac. Do you remember yourself at Alice's age?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「忘れてるなら想像してちょうだい。あのぐらいの歳の女の子が、親の言いつけを破ってこっそり部屋から逃げだしてくるのに、一体どれほどの勇気が必要だったでしょうね」
lines.english: “If you've forgotten, then imagine. How much courage must it have taken a girl that age to disobey her parents and sneak out of her room?”

lines.japanese: 俺は顔を上向きに倒し、夜空に鼻息ひとつを吹きだした。
lines.english: I tilted my head back and snorted once into the night sky.

lines.japanese: このときの感情を、俺は上手く伝えられない。ただなんとなく、今日はアヤトリィかシリトリィかダルマサンガー・コロンブスでもやればよかったなあと思った。
lines.english: I can't properly describe what I felt. I only found myself wishing we'd played Cat's Cradley, Wordy Chain, or Red Light, Columbus today.

lines.japanese: 「まあでも、ほとぼりが冷めりゃ、またひょっこり遊びに来んだろ。なあ」
lines.english: “Still, once things cool down, she'll turn up to play again. Right?”

lines.japanese: 「そうね。そのときはたっぷり遊んであげてね。もちろん不健全な遊びはダメよ」
lines.english: “Yes. And when she does, play with her all you like. No unwholesome games, naturally.”

lines.japanese: 「しねえよ。つか、他人事みたいに言うなよ、おまえも遊ぶんだろ。あいつ、いつかおまえに睨めっこで勝つッつーて張りきってたぞ」
lines.english: “I wouldn't. And don't talk like you're not involved. You'll play too. She was all fired up about beating you at a staring contest someday.”

lines.japanese: 「フフ、無理よ。あの子はこの先どんどん綺麗になっちゃうし、それにアタシは──」
lines.english: “Mmm. Impossible. She'll only grow lovelier from here, and I—”

lines.japanese: マルチネスは不意に言葉を止め、ぷかぷかと煙でドーナツを作っていた。
lines.english: Martinez broke off and began blowing rings of smoke into the air.

lines.japanese: 「──ねえ、ドラちゃん。アナタ、懐郷って言葉をご存知？」
lines.english: “—tell me, Drac. Have you ever heard the word *kaikyō*?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: なんだこのおっさん。アリスもいないのに突然クイズゲームかよ。
lines.english: What was with this old man? Alice wasn't even here, and suddenly it was quiz time again?

lines.japanese: 「カイキョー。なんだソレ。英語か」
lines.english: “Kai-what? Is that English?”

lines.japanese: 「懐郷。英語ではＨｏｍｅ　ｓｉｃｋと言うわ。この国のひとには、何故かそっちの方が浸透してるみたいね」
lines.english: “*Kaikyō*: longing for home. In English, *homesick*. Oddly enough, people in this country seem to know the English better.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、そりゃホームシックぐらい知ってるよ。カイキョーは聞いたことないけど」
lines.english: “Oh, sure, I know *homesick*. Never heard *kaikyō*.”

lines.japanese: 「フフ、いい言葉じゃない。せっかくの美しい日本語ですもの、覚えておきなさい」
lines.english: “Mmm. It's a beautiful word, isn't it? Good Japanese like that deserves to be remembered.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　べつにホームシックはホームシックでいいじゃん。つか何、それがどうしたの」
lines.english: “Huh? *Homesick* works fine. Anyway, what's this about?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、実はアタシ、ぼちぼちロスに帰ろうと思うの」
lines.english: “The truth is, I think it's about time I went home to Los Angeles.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”
“WHAT?!”

lines.japanese: 「あら嬉しい。意外と驚いてくれるのね」
lines.english: “My, how sweet. You're more surprised than I expected.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、何その重大発表。おまえソレ、どんだけサラリと言ってのけてんだよ。なんだよ、どういうこと」
lines.english: What? What's with dropping a huge announcement like that? How can you say it so casually? What? What happened?

lines.japanese: 「実は、アタシが救急で運ばれたときね、病院が本国の連絡先に知らせちゃったの。ああほら、向こうとしちゃ、アタシって消息不明の天才デザイナーじゃない？」
lines.english: “When I was rushed to the hospital, they contacted the people listed back home. You see, over there I'm a missing genius of a designer.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、知らねえよ。いや、聞いた気もするけど、あんま信じてなかった」
lines.english: “How should I know? No—I feel like you told me, but I didn't really believe you.”

lines.japanese: 「それで事務所の若い子──まあ、専属のアシスタントっていうか、いわゆる弟子みたいな子たちなんだけど、彼らが飛行機スッとばして病院まで駆けつけてくれて。帰ってきてくれって泣きながら言うのよう」
lines.english: So the young people at the studio—well, they're more like dedicated assistants, or what you'd call apprentices—they jumped on planes and rushed to the hospital. They were crying and asking me to come back.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、マジで？　うそ、おま、マジですごいやつだったの？」
lines.english: “Wait, seriously? No way. Were you actually somebody incredible?”

lines.japanese: やべ、俺ぜんぜん分かんなかった。あのパチモンくせえシルバーアクセ、実はすげえ高値が付くのか？
lines.english: Damn. I hadn't had a clue. Did that knockoff-looking silver jewelry secretly fetch incredible prices?

lines.japanese: と思って財布に手を伸ばしたが、俺の思考は読まれていたようだ。
lines.english: I started reaching for my wallet, but Martinez seemed to read my thoughts.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ごめんなさい、売ってた品は良いトコ値段相応よ。銀細工はただの趣味だから。デザイナーはデザイナーでも、アタシの専門は空間デザインなの」
lines.english: “Oh, I'm sorry. The things on this stall are worth about what I charge, at best. Silverwork is only a hobby. I am a designer, but spatial design is my field.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、空間デザイン。あー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, spatial design. Sure.”

lines.japanese: なんだかよく分かんねえ。でもシッタカぶって適当な相槌を打っておいた。
lines.english: I had no idea what that meant, but I pretended I did and offered a suitably vague response.

lines.japanese: 「でね、その子たちが言うには、アタシを国外追放した例のお偉いサンが失脚したらしいのよ。一方じゃ、現場にプエルトリコ系のスタッフが増えて、前よりアタシたちの発言力が増してるっていうし」
lines.english: “And according to them, the big shot who had me driven out of the country has fallen from power. Meanwhile, there are more Puerto Rican staff on the ground now, and people like us have more of a voice than before.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……マルチネスって、アメリカ追いだされたから日本に来たんだ」
lines.english: “Huh... So you came to Japan because America ran you out.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、実はそうなの」
lines.english: “Yeah, actually, that’s true.”

lines.japanese: 「んん……たしか、東洋美術を民間レベルで実地検分うんぬんとか聞いてたような……」
lines.english: “Hmm... I thought you said something about conducting a private, firsthand survey of Eastern art...”

lines.japanese: 「それは嘘じゃないけど、後付けの理由だわ。ほほ、その前にね、意地悪なスポンサーに仕事いっさい回してもらえなくなっちゃった、っていう残念な経緯があったの」
lines.english: “That wasn't a lie, but it was a reason I tacked on afterward. Before that, a nasty sponsor had made sure no work came my way at all. A regrettable little history.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで。そうだったんだ」
lines.english: “Seriously. I had no idea.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさいね、隠してて。いつか言おうと思ってたんだけど、そんな湿っぽい話、いざとなるとなかなか機会がなくてね」
lines.english: Sorry for hiding it. I kept meaning to tell you, but with a sappy story like that, you never find the right time once the moment comes.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　いや、べつに嘘ついてたわけでもねーんだし、謝るこっちゃねーだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? You didn't exactly lie. Nothing to apologize for.”

lines.japanese: 「違うの。まだドラちゃんと出会う前、この国に来たばっかりのころのアタシには、まだつまらないプライドがあったのよ。だからそのころは、見栄を張ってひた隠しにしてたの。これは沈黙の嘘ってやつよ」
lines.english: “No. When I first came to this country, before I met you, I still had my petty pride. So I put on airs and kept it desperately hidden. A lie told with silence.”

lines.japanese: 外人は外人みたいに肩をすくめた。
lines.english: The foreigner shrugged like a foreigner.

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿だったのよ。生まれで区別されるような体制に弾かれて、そんな理不尽を誰より憎んでいたのに──」
lines.english: “I was a fool. A system that separated people by birth had cast me out, and no one hated that injustice more than I did—”

lines.japanese: 「──なのに、あのころのアタシったら、この国のひとたちには笑われたくないなんて、そんな恥ずかしい考えが頭の隅にあったんでしょうね」
lines.english: “—and yet, back then, some shameful corner of me still thought, 'I don't want the people of this country laughing at me.'”

lines.japanese: 「フフ、この国で最初に覚えたのがこんな日本語で良かったわ。お陰でみんなが笑ってくれた。天才なんて呼ばれて勘違いしてたアタシの鼻を、アナタたち日本人がバッキバキにへし折ってくれたわけ。ほほほ」
lines.english: “Mmm. I'm glad this was the first kind of Japanese I learned. It made everyone laugh. I'd let being called a genius go to my head, and you Japanese snapped that proud nose of mine clean in two. Ho ho ho.”

lines.japanese: 「それからは視野が広がって、色々なものを受けいれることが出来るようになって。正直に言ってね、ステイツで小さくまとまってたころより、今ならとびきりのいい仕事ができると思うの」
lines.english: “After that, my world grew wider. I learned to accept all sorts of things. Honestly, I think I could do far better work now than when I was keeping myself small in the States.”

lines.japanese: 「本当はあの国へ戻るのちょっぴり恐いのだけど、でも挑んでみたい──ううん、挑んでくるわ」
lines.english: “The truth is, returning to that country frightens me a little. But I want to try—no. I am going to.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……」
俺にはふーん以外の言葉が思いつかなかった。
lines.english: I could think of nothing to say but *huh*.

lines.japanese: しばらく後ろ頭をがしがし掻いて、そっかーとか、じゃ頑張れとか、そんなような短い言葉をいくつか吐いただけだった。
lines.english: I scratched hard at the back of my head for a while and only spat out a couple short things. ‘Oh, yeah?’ ‘Well, good luck.’ Stuff like that.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、なに……あの、アレ……だっておまえ、飛行機代とかあんの」
lines.english: “Wait, what... I mean... Do you even have the airfare?”

lines.japanese: 「ないけど、弟子たちが連れて帰ってくれるんだもの。ウフ、心配は無用よ」
lines.english: “No, but my apprentices are taking me home. Mmm. No need to worry.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、心配はしてねーけどさ」
lines.english: “I'm not worried.”

lines.japanese: どんな顔をしたらいいか分からず、俺は顎の下にウメボシを作ってそっぽを向いた。
lines.english: Not knowing what face to make, I bunched the flesh beneath my chin into a wrinkled little pickled plum and looked away.

lines.japanese: 「はあ、ドラちゃんに会えなくなることだけが心残りだわ」
lines.english: “Ah, Drac. My one regret is that I won't be able to see you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: マルチネスじゃない名前で先生と呼ばれる、オシャレでスタイリッシュなマルチネスを想像した。
lines.english: I imagined a chic, stylish Martinez back home, going by a name other than Martinez and being addressed as a master.

lines.japanese: オシャレでスタイリッシュな事務所を拠点に、オシャレでスタイリッシュな仲間と共に、なんだかよく分かんねえオシャレでスタイリッシュな仕事をばりばりこなして行くのだろう。信じてやっても俺に害はない。
lines.english: They'd probably work out of a stylish studio with stylish friends, doing all kinds of stylish work I didn't really get, full steam ahead. Didn't hurt me to believe it.

lines.japanese: 「あらやだ、そんな寂しい顔しないで」
lines.english: “Oh, don't look so lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「してねえよ」
lines.english: “I'm not.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫、いまのアタシの実力はグローバル級だから。日本で仕事することになったら、余暇としてまたここで露店でも開いてあげるわ」
lines.english: “Don't worry. My abilities are global-class now. If work brings me back to Japan, I'll open another street stall here in my spare time.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ。いつンなるやら。それにどうせアクセの方は才能ねーだろ、おまえ」
lines.english: “Hah. We’ll see when that happens. Besides, you’ve got no talent for jewelry.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ！　本当に失礼なイエローモンキーね！　いまだにアタシの芸術が理解できないっていうの！　見てらっしゃい、半年後にはアナタごときじゃ買えないほどの値段が付くようになってるんだから！」
lines.english: “My! What a rude yellow monkey! You still can’t appreciate my art? Just you wait. In six months these pieces will cost more than the likes of you can afford!”

lines.japanese: 「だけど今なら、友人特価の２千円で譲ってあげる。ウフ、お得な話だと思うけど、どうする？」
lines.english: “But today, I'll let you have this one for the special friendship price of two thousand yen. Hee-hee. A bargain, don't you think?”

lines.japanese: 「こうする」
lines.english: “Like this.”

lines.japanese: 俺はマルチネスが差しだしたマットなシルバーネックレスを地面へ落とした。やつは慌てて拾いあげ、傷がないか裏・表・裏・表と繰りかえし確かめていた。
lines.english: I dropped the matte silver necklace Martinez offered me onto the pavement. In a panic, Martinez snatched it up and checked for scratches: back, front, back, front.

lines.japanese: 「さて、そろそろ行くか」
lines.english: “Right. Time I got going.”

lines.japanese: 若干の空腹感があった。バイト前に軽くなにか入れておこう。
lines.english: I was a little hungry. Better put something light in my stomach before work.

lines.japanese: 「またな」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 旅立つ友人に餞別の目潰しピースを送った。
lines.english: I sent my departing friend off with the parting gift of an eye-gouging V-sign.

lines.japanese: するとキャラメル色の友人は、唇を横へ広げて歯茎を覗かせた。
lines.english: My caramel-colored friend stretched his lips into a grin that showed his gums.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、またね」
lines.english: “Yes. See you around.”

lines.japanese: たやすく記憶に焼きついてしまう、ピースフルな外人スマイル。
lines.english: A peaceful foreigner’s smile, the kind that etched itself effortlessly into memory.

lines.japanese: マルチネスと別れたあと、駅からの目抜き通りを下流に向かって進んだ。
lines.english: After leaving Martinez, I made my way downstream along the main street from the station.

lines.japanese: たまには新しいメシ屋でも開拓するか、とも思いつつ、しかし見慣れたラーメン屋台が目に入ると結局そっちへ足が向かってしまう。
lines.english: I thought about trying somewhere new for dinner, but when the familiar ramen cart came into view, my feet took me there as usual.

lines.japanese: 美味くて安くて居心地がいい、そんな三拍子そろった店のせいで、俺の飲食店に関する冒険心はずいぶん痩せほそってしまった。
lines.english: Tasty, cheap, comfortable. Thanks to a place that hit all three, my urge to try new restaurants had gotten pretty damn skinny.

lines.japanese: 「らっしゃい」
lines.english: “Welcome!”

lines.japanese: カウンター席の前に立った瞬間、威勢のよい声に出迎えられた。
lines.english: The moment I stepped up to the counter, a booming voice greeted me.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、ドラか」
lines.english: “Oh. It’s only you, Drac.”

lines.japanese: なんだ、と言いつつ頬の肉が微妙にほころんでる。ちょうど話相手でも欲しかったんだろうか。
lines.english: He said ‘What?’ but the corners of his cheeks loosened a little. Maybe he'd wanted someone to talk to.

lines.japanese: 「うす。どう、繁盛してる」
lines.english: “Hey. Business good?”

lines.japanese: 「見ての通りだ」
lines.english: “See for yourself.”

lines.japanese: メンマがテーブル席を目で指す。俺はちらりと振りかえった。母子連れらしき二人組が、どんぶりに顔を埋めて貪るようにラーメンを食らっていた。
lines.english: Menma pointed toward the tables with his eyes. I glanced back. What looked like a mother and child had their faces buried in their bowls, devouring their ramen.

lines.japanese: 以上。現在の来客者数、カウンター席の俺を含めて計三名。
lines.english: End of list. Current customer count: three, including me at the counter.

lines.japanese: 「大繁盛だな」
lines.english: “Business is booming.”

lines.japanese: 「え、これって繁盛してるんだ」
lines.english: “Wait, this counts as booming?”

lines.japanese: 「うちはマスコミを味方に付けてる有名店じゃないんだ、これだけ賑わえば上等だろ」
lines.english: “We’re not some famous joint with the press behind us. This much bustle is plenty.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ職人のくせして、そういう環境のせいにすんなよ」
lines.english: “You're supposed to be a craftsman. Don't blame the environment.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、今日のうお座はポジティブシンキングが成功の秘訣らしくてな」
lines.english: “Well, apparently positive thinking is today's key to success for Pisces.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ角刈りのくせして、そういう女くさい雑誌見んなよ」
lines.english: “A man with a crew cut like yours shouldn't be reading girly magazines.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まったくおまえの言うとおりだ。愛され上手ブルボンヌ冴子のスピリチュアル恋愛ラビリンスはとくにひどかった。どの回答も隅から隅まで男をなめくさっていやがった」
lines.english: “You're absolutely right. Saeko Bourbonne's *Spiritual Labyrinth of Romance for the Adeptly Adored* was particularly vile. Every last answer treated men like dirt from one edge of the page to the other.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、隅から隅まで読むなよ。その時点でもう雑誌社に踊らされてんじゃねーか」
lines.english: “Then don't read every page. By that point, the publisher's already got you dancing on its strings.”

lines.japanese: 「フン、知ったことかよ。あの香水くせえアバズレ女ども、あまりにまどろっこしいこと言いやがるもんだから、その場で張ったおしてビリビリに破りすててやったぜ」
lines.english: “Hmph. Like I care. Those perfume-reeking harpies kept spouting such maddeningly roundabout garbage, I slapped the thing down on the spot and tore it to shreds.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、男らしい。いいじゃん、それでこそ俺たちの大将だよ」
lines.english: “Whoa. Manly. Now that's our chief.”

lines.japanese: 「そしたらパルに怒られた」
lines.english: “Then Paru got mad at me.”

lines.japanese: 「雑誌パル姐のかよ」
lines.english: “It was Paru's magazine?”

lines.japanese: 「俺は男の尊厳を守っただけなのに、あの小うるせえ女がガタガタ喚くもんだから、俺はクソ雑誌の税込価格７８０円分の小銭を野郎の足元に叩きつけて『すっこんでろ、これで文句はねえだろ』と怒鳴りつけてやった」
lines.english: “All I did was defend the dignity of men. But that nagging woman wouldn't stop squawking, so I hurled exactly 780 yen in change—the trashy rag's tax-inclusive price—at her feet and roared, ‘Pipe down! There. No complaints now!’”

lines.japanese: 「うお、かっけー。さすがメンマだ。そんでどうした」
lines.english: “Damn, that's cool. Classic Menma. Then what?”

lines.japanese: 「うむ……文句はあったらしい。しばらく揉めたのち、最終的に俺は小銭を拾って本屋へ走ることとなった」
lines.english: “Mm... Apparently she still had complaints. After some argument, I ultimately picked up the coins and ran to the bookstore.”

lines.japanese: 「弱っ」
lines.english: “Weak.”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ない、あのまま口論を続けていたら、俺の右手は今ごろピンクに染まっていただろう」
lines.english: “I had no choice. If we'd kept arguing, my right hand would be stained pink by now.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、おまえもいずれ分かるさ。本当の男に必要なものは、殴りとばす強さより殴られる勇気なのかもしれない」
lines.english: “You'll understand one day, Drac. Perhaps what a true man needs is less the strength to strike than the courage to be struck.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、なんだこのおっさん。なんか締まらないズッコケ話を、背中で語る男の美学的なまとめにすり替えようとしてんぞ」
lines.english: “Listen to him. He’s trying to turn a pathetic pratfall into the sort of rugged wisdom a man delivers with his back turned.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえ。いいから早く。注文」
lines.english: “Shut up. Hurry up and order.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そんじゃいつもの。油多めで」
lines.english: “Fine. The usual. Extra oil.”

lines.japanese: 「おう。まあ、ゆっくりしていけ」
lines.english: “Right. Stay awhile.”

lines.japanese: 「そのつもりだよ。いや、さっきマルチネスたちと会ってさ……おう、ちょーちょーメンマ、ちょっと話あんだけどいい」
lines.english: “That's the plan. I just ran into Martinez and the others... Hey, Menma, hold up. Got something I wanna talk about. You got a minute?”

lines.japanese: 「よくないな。俺がおまえと話したら誰がラーメンを作るんだ。おいパル、ちょっと相手してやってくれ」
lines.english: “No. If I talk to you, who makes the ramen? Hey, Paru. Keep him company.”

lines.japanese: 「んっ、呼んだかい」
lines.english: “Hm? Did you call me?”

lines.japanese: 「って、あんたいたのかよ」
lines.english: “Wait, you were here?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、隼人さんだー、おばんですー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, Hayatooo. Evenin' to yaaa.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえもかよ」
lines.english: “You too?”

lines.japanese: 母子連れの客だと思ってたら……こいつらだったのか……。
lines.english: I'd thought the customers were a mother and child... So that's who they were...

lines.japanese: 「ドラが話あるらしいぞ」
lines.english: “Drac says he's got something to discuss.”

lines.japanese: メンマは俺の前にお冷やを置くと、一歩引いて調理に取りかかった。俺はコップを持ってテーブル席へ移動した。
lines.english: Menma set a glass of water in front of me and stepped back to cook. I took it over to the table.

lines.japanese: 「なんだい、話って」
lines.english: “So what did you want to discuss?”

lines.japanese: パルさんが広げていたファッション誌を閉じる。鳴はずるずる箸を進めながら、片手で俺へ丸椅子を勧めた。俺はラーメンのついでか。
lines.english: Paru closed the fashion magazine she'd spread open. Still slurping noodles, Naru used her free hand to offer me a stool. Nice to know I ranked somewhere below the ramen.

lines.japanese: 「いや、あのさ。パルさん、マルチネスの件聞いてる」
lines.english: “Well. Paru, did you hear about Martinez?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、アメリカ帰るって話だろ」
lines.english: “Yeah. That he's going back to America, right?”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱもう知ってたか」
lines.english: “So you already knew.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、思えばアレだよな……ここ最近、この屋台に全員が集まること少なくなってきたよな」
lines.english: “You know, come to think of it... We haven't all ended up at this cart much lately, have we?”

lines.japanese: 「全員ってなんだい。誰かが声かけて、せーのでここに集まるなんてこと、今までだってなかったろ？」
lines.english: What do you mean, ‘everyone’? It's not like somebody ever called us all and said, ‘Ready, set, meet here!’ We never did that before, did we?

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからソレだよ。その、なんつーか、自然に集まるってことがなくなったっつーか。前までは、なんとなく来りゃ、なんとなくみんな揃ってたのにさ」
lines.english: “No, that's what I mean. I dunno. It's like we stopped gathering naturally. Before, if you wandered over for no reason, somehow everybody'd be here.”

lines.japanese: 「ほおー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺の言いたいことは伝わったのか。パルさんは頬杖をついた。
lines.english: Maybe she understood me. Paru rested her cheek on one hand.

lines.japanese: 「ま、俺らもぼちぼち解散か」
lines.english: “Well. Guess our little group is about ready to break up.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、それは困りますよー」
lines.english: “Nooo, I don't want that.”

lines.japanese: ラーメンに集中していたはずの鳴が話に加わってきた。あ、聞いてなかったわけじゃなくて、旧知同士の会話だと思って遠慮してたのか。
lines.english: Naru, who I thought was focused on her ramen, joined in. Oh, it wasn't that she hadn't been listening. She'd just held back because she thought two old friends were talking.

lines.japanese: 「なんであんたが困ンだい」
lines.english: “Why would that be a problem for you?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いえ、私もこれから足しげく通おうと思ってた矢先だったのでー」
lines.english: “Well, I was just about to start coming here regularly.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか、俺が来いって言ったんだもんな。悪りい、なんかタイミング遅かったみたい。どうもみんな足が遠のいてきちゃって……」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I'm the one who told you to come. Sorry. Looks like your timing was a little late. Everybody's kinda stopped coming...”

lines.japanese: 「いや、最初に足が遠くなったのはおまえだろ、ドラ」
lines.english: “You were the first one to stop coming, Drac.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 店主が出来たてのラーメンを運んできた。俺が呆けていたら、鳴が丼の縁にそっと割り箸を置いてくれた。どーも。目で礼をいう。
lines.english: The proprietor carried over my freshly made ramen. While I sat there blankly, Naru gently laid a pair of disposable chopsticks across the bowl's rim. *Thanks,* I said with my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「パルは気付いてるだろ。ここんとこプラチナたちも顔を見せる日が減ってきたけど、減少率で言やドラが一番だ」
lines.english: Paru's noticed too. Platinum and the others come around less lately, but if we're talking biggest drop, Drac wins.

lines.japanese: 「え、そうだっけ……？」
lines.english: “Has it...?”

lines.japanese: 「良いことなんじゃないか。何かは知らないが、それだけ他に時間を割くことが増えたんだろう」
lines.english: “Isn't that good? I don't know what they are, but it means you've found more things to spend your time on.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まあ……そうなのかな……」
lines.english: “Mm... Maybe...”

lines.japanese: 「ふん。こっちとしちゃ、小っぽけな屋台の数少ない常連だ、結構な痛手だけどな」
lines.english: “Hmph. From where I stand, you're one of the few regulars at this little cart. Losing you hurts.”

lines.japanese: 責めてるみたいな口ぶりだったけど、愛嬌のないこの男にしては珍しく口の端が上がっていた。
lines.english: It sounded accusatory, but for once one corner of the charmless man's mouth had turned upward.

lines.japanese: 「なるほどねぇ、そろそろ移りかわりの時期にきてんのかな」
lines.english: “I see. Maybe we're coming to another season of change.”

lines.japanese: 「移りかわり？」
lines.english: “Season of change?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、これが不思議なもんでね。ここに集まる面子ってなあ、ある時期パァーッと盛りあがるんだけど、なんだかんだで長くは続かないのさ。その期間ってなァ、大体いつもこンぐらいでね」
lines.english: “Yeah. Funny thing about the crowd that gathers here. Every so often it swells into something lively, but one thing and another happen, and it never lasts. And it always seems to last about this long.”

lines.japanese: 「職場が変わったり、生活が変わったり、他にもまあ、いろいろあるからな。それは仕方ない。みんなの再出発やリタイアを見守ってるうち、気付いたら俺とパルだけ最古参になっちまってた」
lines.english: “People change jobs. Their lives change. Plenty else happens too. Can't be helped. I watched everybody make a new start or bow out, and before I knew it, Paru and I were the old guard.”

lines.japanese: 「やだね、そんな誉めるんじゃないよ」
lines.english: “Oh, stop. Don't praise me like that.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、どっちかっつーと不名誉なことじゃね？」
lines.english: “Pretty sure that was closer to an insult.”

lines.japanese: 「だから次は、おまえの周りにひとが集まるのかもしれないぞ、鳴」
lines.english: “So perhaps you'll be the one people gather around next, Naru.”

lines.japanese: 「は！？　わた、私ですかっ？」
lines.english: “What?! M-me?”

lines.japanese: 予想外のところで自分の名前が飛びだして、鳴は大いにうろたえていた。
lines.english: Hearing her name from that unexpected quarter left Naru badly flustered.

lines.japanese: 「ドラたちは離れてく時期みてえだが、おまえはこれからなんだろ、新人」
lines.english: “Drac and his lot may be reaching the time to leave, but you're only beginning, aren't you, rookie?”

lines.japanese: 「おっ、じゃあ、あんたの仇名を決めないとね。ここじゃ仲間同士は仇名で呼びあうってえ寸法よ」
lines.english: Ooh, then we gotta decide your nickname. Around here, buddies call each other by nicknames—that's how it goes.

lines.japanese: 「閉鎖的だよなー、はは、嫌いじゃなかったけど」
lines.english: “Pretty closed-off, huh? Ha ha. I didn't hate it, though.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのう、じゃあ、これからは夜にお腹が空いたらここに来ますね私ー」
lines.english: “Um, well, then whenever I get hungry at night, I'll come here from now on.”

lines.japanese: 「うちのクレープも忘れないでくれよ、なッ！」
lines.english: “Don't forget my crêpes either, you hear?”

lines.japanese: 「うはー、今日からカロリー計算帳つけることにしますー」
lines.english: “Ooh. Starting today, I'm keeping a calorie ledger.”

lines.japanese: そう言いつつスープを残さず飲みほそうと丼を持ちあげるこの女は、ダイエットなんか成功しないだろうと思った。案の定、亜衣ちゃんも道連れだとかなんとかパルさんに訴えていた。
lines.english: She said that while raising the bowl to drain every last drop of broth. I had my doubts about her diet. Sure enough, she started urging Paru to drag Ai into it with her.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、それも今年いっぱいまでの話なんだけどな」
lines.english: “Though that's only true through the end of this year.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なんだよそれ。縁起でもねえな、この屋台閉めちゃうようなこと言うなよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that supposed to mean? Don't say ominous crap like you're closing the cart.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そういうことだ」
lines.english: “No. That's exactly what I mean.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 思わず重い声が出てしまった。
lines.english: My voice came out heavier than I meant it to.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだそりゃ」
lines.english: “...What the hell?”

lines.japanese: この男が冗談を言うとも思えない。俺は我知らず箸を止めていた。
lines.english: This wasn't a man given to jokes. Before I knew it, my chopsticks had stopped.

lines.japanese: だがそんな俺を見て、鉄面皮で通っていた店主が唇を大きく広げて笑う。
lines.english: At the sight of me, however, the famously stone-faced proprietor split into a broad grin.

lines.japanese: 「実は俺な、来年から店を持つことになったんだ」
lines.english: “Truth is, I'm getting a place of my own next year.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺は間抜けなツラをしていたようだ。横でパルさんが笑いだした。くそ、てめえ知ってたのかよ。
lines.english: I must have looked spectacularly stupid, because Paru started laughing beside me. Damn it. You knew, didn't you?

lines.japanese: 「こっちの界隈でいくつか店をプロデュースしてる偉いさんがいてな、客として何度もうちに足を運んでいたらしいんだ。なんでも俺の腕に惚れこんでくれたらしい、先週声をかけられた」
lines.english: “There's a big shot producing several restaurants around here. Apparently he'd come by as a customer more than once. Says he fell in love with my cooking. He approached me last week.”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん悩みはしたんだが、せっかくの機会だろ。いろいろ話していくうちに信用できることも分かったし、体を預けて店長としてやってみることにした」
lines.english: “I gave it plenty of thought, naturally, but an opportunity like this doesn't come often. The more we talked, the more I saw he was someone I could trust, so I decided to put myself in his hands and give running the place a try.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、すごいすごい、おめでとうございますー！」
lines.english: “Wow! Amazing! Congratulations!”

lines.japanese: 「おおすげえ、メンマすげえじゃん。おまえすげえよ、ほんとすげえ」
lines.english: “Holy hell, Menma, that's incredible. You're incredible. Seriously. Just incredible.”

lines.japanese: 気の利いた言葉は何も思いつかなかった。俺はメンマの体を景気よくバンバン叩いた。これで充分だ。口ベタ同士、これだけで言いたいことは伝わるだろう。
lines.english: I couldn't think of anything clever. I gave Menma a few hard, hearty thumps. That was enough. Neither of us was much good with words; he'd get what I meant from that.

lines.japanese: 自分の城を構えるメンマの戦いは、むしろこれからなのかもしれない。
lines.english: Maybe Menma's fight to build his own castle was only starting now.

lines.japanese: でも俺たちの大将ならきっとやってくれる。俺たちがふらりと帰ってこられる場所を、この先ずっと守りつづけてくれる。確証もないのにそんな確信があった。
lines.english: But our chief would pull it off. He'd keep a place for us, somewhere we could wander home to, far into the future. I had no evidence and complete faith.

lines.japanese: 「チキショー、私も負けてらんないやね。友達とスイーツショップ開く話、そろそろ本格的に考えはじめないと──」
lines.english: “Damn it, I can't let him leave me behind. I'd better get serious about that sweets shop my friend and I have discussed opening—”
“—Whoops.”

lines.japanese: 「ああごめん、電話が入っちまったい。ちょいと抜けるよ」
lines.english: “Sorry. Got a call. I'm stepping away a moment.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが席を立ったことで、いったん空気が落ちついた。ぬるい水を喉に通したあと、鳴が始めに口を開く。
lines.english: Once Paru left the table, the air settled. After sending some lukewarm water down her throat, Naru spoke first.

lines.japanese: 「新しいお店はどちらになる予定なんですかー」
lines.english: “Where will the new restaurant be?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、花水木通りから一本入ったとこでな。詳しい場所は、ビラでも作るからそのとき確認してくれ」
lines.english: “One street over from Flowering Dogwood Street. I’ll make flyers, so you can check the address then.”

lines.japanese: 「店の名前はもう決まってんの」
lines.english: “You got a name yet?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラーメンだ」
lines.english: “Drac-men.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　ださっ。なんだそりゃ」
lines.english: “What? That's awful. What the hell kind of name is that?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラーメン。ドラの人徳にあやかろうと思ってな」
lines.english: “Drac-men. Thought I'd borrow some of Drac's personal magnetism.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、素敵なお名前ですねー」
lines.english: “Oh, what a lovely name.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいや、ツッコむとこだろそれは」
lines.english: “No, no, no. That's your cue to call him out.”

lines.japanese: 「看板の目印は、目付きの悪いドラキュラがラーメン食ってる絵だ。横にブッ殺すぞコノヤロウと英語で添えようと思ってる」
lines.english: “The sign will show a mean-looking Dracula eating ramen. Beside him, in English: ‘I'LL KILL YOU, ASSHOLE.’”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　ふざけんなコラ、ソレ俺の事務所は通したのか。肖像権の侵害とかで訴えッかんな、てめ示談にしたけりゃ無料券よこせブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “The fuck? Don't screw with me. Did you clear that through my agency? I'll sue your ass for using my likeness. Wanna settle, hand over some free-meal tickets. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「あとは鳴の仇名も決めないとな」
lines.english: “We need a nickname for Naru too.”

lines.japanese: 「聞けよおっさん」
lines.english: “Listen to me, old man.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そーですねー、たとえば私レディとかマドンナとかそっち系ですよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. I suppose mine should be something like Lady or Madonna.”

lines.japanese: 「ハハ、そうだな」
lines.english: “Ha-ha. Sure.”

lines.japanese: 「おっさんおっさん。ハハじゃねーよ、こいつ付けあがるから、無責任な相槌打つのとかやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Old man. Hey, old man. Don't ‘ha-ha, sure’ her. You'll encourage her. Could you stop agreeing to things without thinking?”

lines.japanese: 「あえて名詞から離れて、セクシーとかコケティッシュとかどうですかねー」
lines.english: “Or we could venture beyond nouns. How about Sexy? Coquettish?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、悪くないんじゃないか」
lines.english: “Well, those aren't bad.”

lines.japanese: 「おっさん。いや、悪いだろ。ありえねーだろ。ちょっとホント頼むからさ──」
lines.english: “Old man. Yes they are. They're impossible. Come on, I'm seriously begging you—”

lines.japanese: 「ちょいとドラ」
lines.english: “Drac. A moment.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ？　なに、いま取り込み中なんだけど」
lines.english: “H-huh? What? I'm kinda busy here.”

lines.japanese: 「いいから電話に出てくれよ。ほれ」
lines.english: “Never mind that. Take the phone. Here.”

lines.japanese: 俺はメンマの太い首に手をかけていたが、パルさんがぐいぐい携帯電話を押しつけてくる。なんだよ、便利屋の仕事ならもう廃業したはずだぞ。
lines.english: I had one hand around Menma’s thick neck, but Paru kept pushing the phone at me. What the hell? I’d closed down the handyman business ages ago.

lines.japanese: しかしパルさんがあまりにしつこいから、もしや重大な事態なのかもと思い、仕方なしに受けとった。
lines.english: But Paru kept insisting, so maybe it was serious, I figured, and took the phone.

lines.japanese: 「ハイもしもしドラーメン……じゃねえよ、誰が目付きの悪いドラキュラだてめ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hello, Drac-men speaking—no, fuck that. Who’re you calling a mean-looking Dracula? I’ll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　いきなり何いってんのおまえ？」
lines.english: “Huh? What the hell are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 電話の相手はチンピラエージだった。俺はパルさんを睨みつけ……ようとしたが、すでに女は逃げていた。
lines.english: The punk on the other end was Eiji. I turned to glare at Paru—or tried to. The woman had already fled.

lines.japanese: くそ……やられた……。
lines.english: Damn it... She got me...

lines.japanese: 「なあ、そんなことよりさあ、ドラに頼みたい仕事あんだよねェ。いや、合法合法！　ぜんぜん怪しくない、ほんと簡単な仕事なんだよ。なあ、引きうけてくれよドラ～」
lines.english: “Hey, never mind that. I've got a little job I want Drac to do. It's legal, it's legal! Nothing shady. Real simple. C'mon, Drac, help me out.”

lines.japanese: 「うっせ、ふざけんなヒモ野郎。成田工務店はもうとっくに廃業してんだよ。長年のご愛顧ありがとうございませんでした。オラ文句ねえな、切んぞ」
lines.english: “Shut up, you freeloading bastard. Narita Construction shut down ages ago. Thank you very much for none of your patronage over the years. There. No complaints? I’m hanging up.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、実は、彼女の誕生日が近付いてンだけどー」
lines.english: “See, the thing is, my girlfriend's birthday is coming up...”

lines.japanese: 「プレゼントにおねだりされちゃったバッグがさあ、なんとかっていうブランドの限定品で、チョー競争率高いのよ。なあドラ、俺の代わりに朝から並んできてくんなぁ～い？」
lines.english: “And the bag she asked for is some limited-edition thing from some brand. Competition's insane. Hey, Drac, wanna line up for me first thing in the morning?”

lines.japanese: 「……おめ、ホントひとの話聞かねえな。あ？　なに、行列に並べだあ？　そんなもんおまえ、自分で並べばいーじゃねえか」
lines.english: “...You really don’t listen to a damn word anyone says, do you? You want me to stand in line? Stand in your own damn line.”

lines.japanese: 「それがね？　俺その日朝イチで、どぉーしても外せない用事があんのよ」
lines.english: “I would, see, but I've got something first thing that morning that I absolutely cannot miss.”

lines.japanese: 「どんな用事」
lines.english: “What’s so important?”

lines.japanese: <8>\「その日、駅前のスロ屋が新装開店でさあ！」
lines.english: “The slot parlor by the station is having its grand reopening that day!”

lines.japanese: 思わず凍ったバナナでやつの頭に釘を打ちつけたくなった。
lines.english: I suddenly wanted to hammer a nail into his skull with a frozen banana.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし？　おいドラ、聞いてる？　俺も正念場なんだよ、なあ頼むよドラ～。ドぉ～んラ～」
lines.english: “Hello? Hey, Drac, listening? This is my moment of truth too. C'mon, I'm begging you, Drac. Draaac. Draaa-aaac.”

lines.japanese: 「♪ドラちゃん、ドラちゃん、ド～ラちゃん　♪パルさんと朝一緒だったド～ラちゃ～ん、パルさんとチュッチュしてたド～ラちゃ～ん……」
lines.english: “♪ Drac dear, Drac dear, Draaac dear! ♪ Drac spent the morning with Paru dear! Drac was kissy-kissy with Paru dear...”

lines.japanese: はあ、アタマ痛てえ……。
lines.english: God, my head hurt...

lines.japanese: 他の誰が変わっても、こいつだけは変わらねえなあ……。
lines.english: Everybody else might change, but this idiot never would.

lines.japanese: 俺はエージの歌声が流れでる携帯電話を、そっとパルさんの耳元に当ててやった。その後やつがどうなったか俺は知らない。
lines.english: I gently held the phone up to Paru’s ear while Eiji was still singing into it. I have no idea what happened to him after that.

lines.japanese: そのあとは鳴を駅まで送ってゆき、夜空を見上げて気合いを入れた。
lines.english: Afterward I walked Naru to the station, looked up at the night sky, and fired myself up.

lines.japanese: 「さて働くぞ」
lines.english: “Right. Time to work.”

lines.japanese: ひとりになった俺はぶらぶらとヒゲカンの待つ現場へ向かった。
lines.english: On my own again, I wandered toward the job site where the Bearded Foreman was waiting.
